Q: Terminating Flask app by Ctrl+C does not trigger KeyboardInterrupt A:

Flask uses werkzeug.serving.run_simple() and it catches KeyboardInterrupt
(to close it "gracefully"/"gently")

in werkzeug.serving.serve_forever()

    def serve_forever(self, poll_interval: float = 0.5) -> None:
        try:
            super().serve_forever(poll_interval=poll_interval)
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
        finally:
            self.server_close()

and werkzeug._reloader.run_with_reloader()

def run_with_reloader(
    main_func: t.Callable[[], None],
    extra_files: t.Iterable[str] | None = None,
    exclude_patterns: t.Iterable[str] | None = None,
    interval: int | float = 1,
    reloader_type: str = "auto",
) -> None:
    """Run the given function in an independent Python interpreter."""
    import signal

    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, lambda *args: sys.exit(0))
    reloader = reloader_loops[reloader_type](
        extra_files=extra_files, exclude_patterns=exclude_patterns, interval=interval
    )

    try:
        if os.environ.get("WERKZEUG_RUN_MAIN") == "true":
            ensure_echo_on()
            t = threading.Thread(target=main_func, args=())
            t.daemon = True

            # Enter the reloader to set up initial state, then start
            # the app thread and reloader update loop.
            with reloader:
                t.start()
                reloader.run()
        else:
            sys.exit(reloader.restart_with_reloader())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass

So app.run() doesn't raise KeyboardInterrupt and you can't catch it.
And you don't have to catch it if you only want to close it "gracefully"/"gently".

Q: How do I isort using ruff? A:

Run Ruff by one command:

ruff check --select I --fix . && ruff format .

Explanation:

  • ruff check : triggers the linter

  • --select I : check isort rules in the I category & I means import sorting

  • --fix : Automatically fixes any import issues found

  • . : targets the current directory & all subdirectories

  • && : if the previous command succeeds then run the next command, otherwise don't run

  • ruff format . : Runs Ruff's code formatter on the entire current directory (.)

Q: Python subclass dircmp A:

methodmap is a class attribute, accessed via self, so if you override that mapping in your subclass definition, e.g.:

class dircmp(filecmp.dircmp):

    def phase3(self) -> None:
        print("subclass phase3 method")
        # ...set whichever attributes you're mapping this to

    methodmap = filecmp.dircmp.methodmap.copy()
    methodmap.update(same_files=phase3, diff_files=phase3, funny_files=phase3)

the subclass's phase3 implementation will be called via the superclass's __getattr__ at the appropriate times.

Q: How to access reference in reusable workflow A:

If you want to call a reusable workflow or action in the same repository at the same reference as yourself (whatever that is), then you can use self-reference syntax (announced here), like this:

      - name: composite action
        uses: $/actions/my-composite-action

Notice the $/ at the start of the cross-reference.

For checking out extra files as part of a reusable workflow, I use a helper action in the same repository:

name: "Internal: Checkout Self"
inputs:
  path:
    default: .self
  sparse-checkout:
    default: null
  repository:
    default: ${{ github.action_repository }}
  ref:
    default: ${{ github.action_ref }}
runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      with:
        path: ${{ inputs.path }}
        sparse-checkout: ${{ inputs.sparse-checkout }}
        repository: ${{ inputs.repository }}
        ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
        persist-credentials: false

That I can then call, perhaps like this:

      - uses: $/.github/internal-actions/checkout-self
        with:
          path: .the_dir
          sparse-checkout: just/this/bit

The only tricky bit is that you can't put ${{ github.action_repository }} and ${{ github.action_ref }} directly in the arguments to the call to actions/checkout due to when the binding of those things happens. I think that's a bug, but others (at GitHub in particular) disagree; still a misfeature at best. Binding in a previous step or as an input bypasses that problem.
